relatedSnapshot.title: Build power dialler session start, pause, resume, and queue building
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12173. For THIS ticket: a power dialler "**session**" = one calling run: a rep pressed Call on a saved view, and the system works through that list. This ticket builds the backend lifecycle: start a session, build its queue from the view, pause, resume, end. "**Materialization**" = copying the view's matching rows into the session's own queue table, done in chunks of ~500 so a 10,000-row list starts Company One (think paginated import, with a stored **cursor** = a bookmark recording how far we've read). "**Controller token**" = a secret that marks WHICH browser tab is allowed to drive the session, so a second tab can't fight the first. Deal views need one extra rule: a deal is a sale, not a person, so we resolve each deal to the actual person to phone (primary linked contact with a phone, else the first linked contact with a phone). Why it matters: this is the spine of the power dialler; the claim/dial logic (next ticket) hangs off the sessions and queues you build here.

**Size:** M/L · **Design:** none · **Blocked by:** ENG-12177
**How it should work (Close reference):** starting a session from a saved list (GIF): <url>

### Overview

An SDR opens a saved contact or deal view and starts power dialling. The server creates their session and builds the calling queue from the view, in the view's order. The rep can pause, resume, or end the run, and can only have one run at a time. Starting again while a run exists gives a choice: pick the old one back up, or start fresh.

### Problem

ENG-12177 gives us the tables but nothing fills them. There is no way to start a session, build the queue from a view, keep the queue topped up for big lists, pause or resume, or stop a rep from running two sessions at once.

### Solution

Build the server-side session lifecycle and queue building. The queue is built from the view in chunks (materialization: copying matching rows from the view into the session's queue), so huge lists start fast and still run to completion. No cap on list size.

Technical notes:

* `dialer.startSession` accepts a contact view or a deal view.
* Deal rows resolve to one person by ONE deterministic rule, acceptance-tested: the deal's primary linked contact IF that contact has a phone; otherwise the first linked contact by creation order that has a phone. That contact's primary number is dialled (locked decision: primary number only in v1). Deals with no linked contact holding a phone get no item (items require `contactId`) and are counted in the phoneless count, never silently dropped.
* Queue building runs server-side through the query-builder internals, NOT paged `getContacts` (its 100-row page cap and permission truncation make it unsafe for queues). Chunked with the stored `materializationCursor` (last sort key plus id tie-breaker for deterministic order). First chunk ~500 rows. Top-up runs inside `claimNext` (the claim-protocol ticket) when pending items drop below ~25.
* Per-session single writer: a session-row lock (`FOR UPDATE`) fences top-up, the 5-minute cron sync, and `syncNow` so they never overlap.
* Session state machine, server-enforced, idempotent transitions: active | paused (reason: user, view_deleted, or access_lost) | completed | abandoned. Completed and abandoned are terminal. An idle worker sweeps BOTH active and paused sessions whose `lastActivityAt` is older than 2 hours straight to abandoned and releases their leases, but never while a live call is bound to the session. Idle expiry is never shown as a pause.
* `lastActivityAt` is refreshed by `claimNext`, `completeItem`, `skipItem`, pause, resume, and heartbeat.
* Starting a session on ANY view while one exists prompts end-or-resume. "Start From Scratch" (and starting on another view) is ONE transaction: mark the old session completed, release the old session's non-live leases in that same transaction, create the fresh session. This satisfies the one-session database rule with no gap. The swap is REFUSED with a clear error while a live call is bound to the old session: end the call first.
* Counts are tracked as separate numbers, not one blended figure:
  * source rows in the view,
  * unique dialable contacts after duplicate collapse (two deals or rows sharing one person become one queue item): this is the primary progress denominator the panel shows,
  * duplicate-collapsed count (how many source rows merged into an existing person),
  * phoneless count (rows with nobody to dial),
  * a cursor-exhausted flag (true once the whole view has been read into the queue).
* Controller fencing lives HERE, not in the later UX ticket. `startSession` and `resumeSession` issue and rotate the `controllerToken` and `controllerGeneration`. Every rep-initiated dialler mutation validates the token server-side from day one. System writers (the sync cron, Twilio callbacks) are trusted paths and never carry the token. The wrap-up/recovery ticket later adds only the takeover UX.
* Permission matrix, gated per action, never as one bundle:
  * Dialling: `FEATURES.POWER_DIALER` feature flag composed with the `voice.make_call` permission.
  * Editing or overriding a call outcome: `manage_call_events` (claim-protocol ticket).
  * Unknown-number quick-create: contact-create rights; without them the flow degrades gracefully (call logs unlinked, no create prompt).
  * Server-side on every mutation: organization membership, session ownership, and saved-view access at start.
  * Verify the intended SDR role holds the full set (`voice.make_call` + `manage_call_events` + contact-create) and document the degraded behavior for each missing capability.

### Scope

* In: `startSession`, pause, resume, end, heartbeat; queue materialization with cursor and top-up trigger contract; session state machine and idle sweep; the deal-to-contact rule; the five count grains; controller token issuance, rotation, and validation; per-action permission gating.
* Out of scope: claiming and completing items (claim-protocol ticket), view sync and the Continue vs Start From Scratch skip rules (queue-sync ticket), all UI, takeover UX.

### Acceptance criteria

 1. When a rep starts a session from a contact view, then a session row and the first ~500 queue items exist in the view's sort order, and the counts and cursor-exhausted flag are correct.
 2. When a rep starts a session from a deal view, then each deal resolves by the rule: primary linked contact if it has a phone, else the first linked contact by creation order with a phone; the chosen contact's primary number is stored; a deal with no linked contact holding a phone creates no item and increments the phoneless count.
 3. When two deals in the view share one contact, then exactly one item exists for that contact, `sourceEntityIds` holds both deals, and the duplicate-collapsed count reflects the merge. Unique dialable contacts is reported as the progress denominator.
 4. When the view has more matches than one chunk, then top-up (triggered from `claimNext` when pending < ~25) continues under the session lock until the cursor is exhausted, with stable order across chunk boundaries, no duplicate items, and no stranded matches.
 5. When a rep with an active or paused session starts a session on any view, then they are prompted to end or resume; if they choose Start From Scratch, then in one transaction the old session becomes completed, its non-live leases are released, and the new session is created.
 6. When a live call is bound to the current session, then Start From Scratch and any cross-view start are refused server-side with a clear error, and nothing changes.
 7. When a session's `lastActivityAt` is older than 2 hours, then the idle worker moves it (active or paused) to abandoned and releases its leases; when a live call is bound, then the sweep skips that session.
 8. When `claimNext`, `completeItem`, `skipItem`, pause, resume, or heartbeat run, then `lastActivityAt` is refreshed.
 9. When a rep-initiated mutation arrives with a stale controller token or generation, then the server rejects it; when `startSession` or `resumeSession` runs, then a fresh token and generation are issued.
10. When the feature flag is off or the caller lacks `voice.make_call`, then every session procedure rejects server-side; when a session, view, or item id from another organization is passed, then the mutation is rejected.
11. When a rep lacks contact-create rights, then unknown-number handling degrades as specified: the call still logs, unlinked, and no create prompt is shown.
12. When the same transition is replayed (duplicate pause, duplicate resume), then the state does not corrupt (idempotent transitions).

### Design (Name 2)

Backend ticket — for reference, the UI this drives: 27 · power dialer preflight (session start, queue counts) and 28 · power dialer active — bottom bar (running session). Full screen map on master ENG-12173.

relatedSnapshot.title: Build the wrap-up window, auto-advance, and session recovery
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12173. For THIS ticket: the "**wrap-up window**" is the short pause after each call where the rep finishes their note and confirms the outcome; then a countdown runs and the next call dials itself. That rhythm (hang up → wrap up → auto-dial next) is what makes it a POWER dialler instead of "click for every call". The recovery half handles real life: browsers crash, laptops sleep, reps open second tabs. The safety machinery for all of that (controller tokens, leases, the live-call registry) is ALREADY BUILT by the earlier backend tickets; you are building only the screens and prompts on top: resume-on-load, "take over here" in a second tab, and clear lost-control states. The one rule to internalize: the next dial fires ONLY after the SERVER confirms the previous call is finished and its outcome is saved. The browser's own "call ended" event opens the wrap-up UI, nothing more. Why it matters: this ticket is the difference between a demo and something SDRs can run for 4 hours straight.

**Size:** M/L · **Design:** needed · **Blocked by:** ENG-12190, ENG-12187, ENG-12185, ENG-12181
**How it should work (Close reference):** pause, Next Call, and taking notes between calls: <url>

### Overview

When a call ends, the rep gets a short wrap-up window: finish the note, confirm the outcome, make quick edits to the lead. Then the dialler moves to the next call on its own after a countdown. The rep can cancel the countdown, change its length, or turn it off entirely. This is what turns the dialler from "click for each call" into a real power dialler. And because browsers crash, laptops sleep, and reps open second tabs, the same ticket gives the rep a clean way back in: reload the page and resume the session, or take over the session from another tab. The safety machinery for recovery already exists on the server; that part of this ticket is only the screens and prompts on top of it.

### Problem

After ENG-12190, reps advance manually only. Close-parity power dialling needs the automatic rhythm: hang up, wrap up, next call, without extra clicks. And once that rhythm exists, a crash or a second tab leaves the rep without a guided way to resume, and without a clear message when another tab holds the session.

### Solution

Wrap-up and auto-advance:

* A wrap-up window after each hang-up: the in-call note continues (from ENG-12181), the outcome is prefilled from the automatic result and confirmed from the fixed v1 list (Answered, No answer, Busy, Left voicemail, Wrong number), and the rep can make quick lead edits.
* Auto-advance countdown: 5 seconds by default, rep-adjustable, cancellable, and it can be turned off (locked decision).
* The countdown starts only after the SERVER confirms the terminal callback and the wrap-up state. It never starts on the browser's call-ended event alone.
* If the rep does not pick a disposition before the advance, the automatic outcome stands and is recorded. This is intended behavior, stated here explicitly.
* If the terminal callback from Twilio is delayed or lost, the window shows a "finishing up" state until the watchdog (the background check that asks Twilio for the true call status) resolves it. No countdown runs and no next dial fires while finishing up.
* The browser's call-ended event may drive UI (opening the wrap-up shell, stopping timers), but the next dial never fires until the server confirms the previous item is terminal AND its disposition is recorded.
* When the rep returns to a view with a recent session, a chooser offers Continue Calling versus Start From Scratch (backend in ENG-12185).

Recovery and takeover, UX only. The fencing mechanism (controller token issuance, rotation, server-side rejection of stale tokens, and the dial-time generation check) already shipped in ENG-12177, ENG-12183, and ENG-12186. System writers (the sync job, Twilio callbacks) are trusted paths that never carry the token. This ticket builds:

* Resume on load: when a page load detects the rep's active session, it offers to resume. Resuming re-claims the current lead or claims the next one.
* Second-tab takeover: a second tab detects that an active controller exists elsewhere and offers "take over here". Taking over rotates the controller token, which fences the old tab out. Takeover is refused while a live browser call is bound to the session, and can be retried once the call ends.
* Lost-control state: the fenced-out tab sees that it no longer controls the session, because the server rejects its stale token.
* Clean exit: ending or leaving the session releases the lease only when no live call exists. The server knows whether a call is live via the live-call registry (its list of calls currently in progress). Lease expiry covers crashes: if the browser dies, leases lapse on their own, with no manual cleanup.

**Technical notes**

* Auto-dial of the next lead goes through the ENG-12187 hooks plus `claimNext`. The server-confirmed wrap-up state (item terminal plus disposition recorded, per ENG-12184) is the only green light.
* Disposition confirmation writes through the authoritative ENG-12175 path (`voice.updateDisposition`); manual always beats automatic.
* Modal built on NiceModal. Known gotcha: NiceModal dialogs render outside the org provider, so org context must be passed as props.
* Permission matrix (wrap-up): confirming or changing an outcome requires `manage_call_events`. A rep without it sees the outcome read-only, the automatic outcome stands, and advancing still works. All mutations validate org membership and session, item, and lease ownership server-side.
* Recovery and takeover screens reuse existing dialogs and banner patterns, no new mockups (pattern-reuse).
* Permission matrix (recovery): resume and takeover call the existing session procedures (ENG-12183), which validate org membership, session ownership, and the feature flag plus `voice.make_call` server-side. Takeover rotates the token server-side; the refusal during a live call is enforced by the server via the live-call registry, never just in the UI.

### Scope

* In: wrap-up window (note continuation, outcome confirm from the fixed list, quick lead edits)
* In: auto-advance countdown with settings (default 5 seconds, adjustable, cancellable, off switch)
* In: server-confirmed advance gating and the "finishing up" state
* In: Continue Calling versus Start From Scratch chooser UI
* In: graceful degrade for reps without the outcome-edit permission
* In: resume-on-load prompt and flow
* In: "take over here" prompt, live-call refusal state, retry after call end
* In: lost-control state in the fenced tab
* In: clean-exit release behavior
* Out of scope: voicemail drop button (RCC 8, additive later), admin-configurable outcome lists (follow-up), any token, lease, or registry mechanics (already shipped in ENG-12177, ENG-12183, ENG-12184, ENG-12186), inbound calls

### Acceptance criteria

 1. When a call ends and the server confirms it is terminal, the wrap-up window shows the note and the outcome prefilled from the automatic result.
 2. When the browser sees the call end but the server has not yet confirmed the terminal callback and wrap-up state, no countdown starts and no next dial fires. The countdown starts only on server confirmation.
 3. When auto-advance is at defaults, the countdown is 5 seconds. The rep can change the length, cancel a running countdown, or turn auto-advance off, and the choice persists for the rep.
 4. When the rep does not pick a disposition before the advance, the automatic outcome stands, is recorded, and the next call proceeds.
 5. When the rep picks a different outcome, it is saved through the authoritative disposition path and beats the automatic one, including against late or duplicate callbacks.
 6. When the terminal callback is delayed or lost, the window shows "finishing up" until the watchdog resolves the call. Only then can wrap-up complete and the next dial fire.
 7. In every case, the next dial fires only after the server confirms the previous item is terminal and its disposition is recorded, even if the browser saw the call end much earlier.
 8. When the rep returns to a view with a recent session, the chooser appears. Continue Calling skips anyone attempted or reached in the last hour. Start From Scratch does not skip them.
 9. When a rep lacks the outcome-edit permission, the outcome shows read-only, the automatic outcome stands, and auto-advance still works.
10. When the rep makes quick lead edits in wrap-up, they save to the lead record.
11. When a rep reloads mid-session, a resume offer appears. Accepting re-claims the current lead or claims the next one, with no stuck state.
12. When a second tab opens the dialler while another tab controls the session, it shows "take over here" instead of silently starting or erroring.
13. When the rep takes over, the controller token rotates. The old tab's next action is rejected by the server and that tab shows it lost control.
14. When a live browser call is bound to the session, takeover is refused with a clear message, and it succeeds once the call has ended.
15. When the rep exits cleanly with no live call, the lease is released immediately. When a live call exists, release waits until the server sees the call end.
16. When the browser crashes, leases expire on their own. After expiry another rep can claim the contact, and the crashed rep can still resume their session.
17. In every recovery case above, enforcement is server-side. Hiding a button is never the protection: a stale-token action sent anyway is rejected by the server.

### Design (Name 2)

* 29 · power dialer outcome — wrap-up — the wrap-up: "How did it go?" outcome chips (Connected / No answer / Left voicemail / Wrong number / Booked meeting), the "when you save this outcome" stage-move + automation preview, note field, **Save & next** / Schedule follow-up
* 28 · power dialer active — bottom bar — the session bar the wrap-up replaces between calls

Full screen map on master ENG-12173.

relatedSnapshot.title: Log why each Power Dialer call is refused
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Why

17 of 33 refused Power Dialer calls between 13 and 19 Oct 2026 log only a bare `VoiceDialAuthorizationError` ("Power dial authorization failed" in Axiom), so we can't tell which check refuses them, and reps lose calls we can't explain or fix.

## What

* Every refusal in `authorizeAndBindPowerDial` and `authorizeOrdinaryBrowserDial` (`apps/web/lib/dialer/authorize-dial.ts`) carries a reason code, logged as the top-level `refusalReason` field: invalid_grant, from_mismatch, destination_mismatch, member_not_found, member_mismatch, voice_access_denied, session_missing, item_missing, session_member_mismatch, caller_id_not_owned, target_not_visible, caller_id_changed, browser_voice_unavailable, do_not_contact, funding_denied, contact_held, calling_policy, call_conflict (with `errorMessage`), invalid_signature, invalid_call_context, unexpected (with `errorName` and, for a TRPCError, `errorCode`).
* When the target is hidden, the log also says why (`targetVisibilityReason`, from `explainCurrentDialerTargetVisibility` in the new `target-visibility.ts`), whether the saved view's filters changed since the session last synced them (`filterSnapshotDrifted`, the same rule queue reconciliation uses before it rewrites the session snapshot), and whether the lead would still pass under the session's own filters (`visibleUnderSessionSnapshot`).
* The caller gets the same generic response as today.

## Lead hypothesis (medium-low confidence)

The visibility check rebuilds filters from the live saved view, not the session's snapshot (confirmed in code: `createDialerFilterSnapshot(view, …)` in `isCurrentDialerTargetVisible`). Name 3's shared view was edited 13 times on 19 Oct, so leads claimed under old filters may be refused. Relative-date filters such as lastTouchAt are the other suspect. The new fields separate the two. Changing the check to use the snapshot is a follow-up, because live re-reads may be how revoked access takes effect.

## Done when

* Unit tests assert each reason code through the logged fields, and a DB test proves drift and the session-snapshot recheck on a real edited view.
* After deploy, one day of Axiom has a non-null `refusalReason` on every "Power dial authorization failed" row, with a breakdown by reason, visibility reason and drift. An empty window is inconclusive.

relatedSnapshot.title: Make the power dialler wait for the rep before calling the next person
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Part of ENG-15216. Reps have used the power dialler once since we moved off Close, so this makes a session safe to work in. The next call waits until the rep has finished, keys do the common actions, and the screen says why a session can't start. It also adds the dialler tracking every later child is measured with.

## Problem

* A 5-second auto-next countdown starts when the call ends. Typing a note, the text box and the Task or Book meeting dialogs don't pause it, so the next call starts mid-note.
* The Start button disappears without a reason when there's no saved view, a flag is off or a caller ID is missing.
* There are no keyboard shortcuts and no Skip button, and pausing comes in four different forms.
* With answer detection on, the dialler hangs up on voicemail and logs "Left voicemail" though nothing was left. The settings text says it "skips voicemail automatically".
* PostHog only records `tool.opened` and `enable_ring_twice` for the dialler.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    A[Call ends] --> B[Server saves result] --> C[5 s countdown] --> D[Next call, even mid-note]
  end
  subgraph After
    E[Call ends] --> F[Rep picks outcome] --> G{Typing or dialog open?}
    G -- no --> H[1.5 s with Undo] --> I[Next call]
    G -- yes --> F
  end
```

## What's included

* **Advance rule:** the queue moves only when the call has ended, an outcome and its required fields are saved, and no note, text box or dialog is open. Then 1.5 s with Undo; Undo can't run once the next dial starts. The 60 s server fallback for reps who walk away stays, but it pauses the session instead of dialling on.
* **Keys:** 1 to 9 for outcomes, S skip, N next, P pause, ? help. Keys are off while typing. One Pause control replaces the four.
* **Skip:** a Skip button wired to the existing skip action.
* **Honest voicemail copy:** the result reads "Voicemail, no message" when the dialler hung up, and the setting describes what it does.
* **Say why Start is missing:** every condition that hides Start shows a reason with a fix link instead.
* **Tracking:** PostHog events `dialler.session_started` (queue or view), `call.placed`, `call.connected`, `call.outcome` (with the outcome).

## Out of scope

* Lock override and idle-hold release tracking (`lock.override`): ENG-15218. It ships with the Call anyway and hold-release actions.
* New queues and the new call screen: ENG-15220.
* Voicemail drop: ENG-12188.

## Done when

* Typing a note or opening Book meeting during wrap-up never starts the next call. How to check: a unit test on the advance hold, and a browser check on a preview.
* Undo within 1.5 s keeps the rep on the same person, and no second call is placed.
* Every condition that blocks Start shows a reason instead of a missing button.
* The four PostHog events (`dialler.session_started`, `call.placed`, `call.connected`, `call.outcome`) land in PostHog from a preview session.

## Implementation context

Code at commit 076050116c: the countdown hold list is in `apps/web/components/crm/power-dialer/use-power-dialer-wrap-up-surface.ts` (around line 76), the countdown in `use-power-dialer-wrap-up.ts`, the server fallback in `apps/web/lib/dialer/call-status.ts`, and the voicemail setting copy in `apps/web/components/crm-v2/settings/phone-calling.tsx`.

relatedSnapshot.title: Keep the power dialler running when a call is refused, with a clear Retry
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

When the phone balance check refuses or times out a call, the power dialler keeps the rep's session going and shows **Retry call** (and Skip), instead of pausing the whole session as "paused by the user".

## Why

Delivers the dialler part of ENG-15760. 33 calls were refused by our answer step between 13 and 19 Oct and left no record. 13 of them also paused the session, and the bar only offers Retry when a call never started (`controller-state.ts`, line 28). On 19 Oct Name 3 had 17 refusals in 3 hours across 7 sessions and made only 11 dialler calls (prod query, power-dialler investigation). Name 3 reported the same wait in ENG-15739: 1 to 2 minutes of dead time, and the only way out was Pause and skip the outcome.

## How it should work

A refused or busy call behaves like a call that never started: the lead stays with the rep, the bar says in plain words that the call did not connect and offers Retry call and Skip lead, and the session is not paused. The rep can dial the next lead within seconds. The exact wording and layout follow what reps said in the Slack reports and tickets.

## Not doing

* Fixing the cause of the refusals: ENG-15760 siblings own the balance check and answer step.
* Closing half-done leads when a session ends (its own sibling ticket).
* The record-session and outcome UI in Anuj's PRs Acquisity/Acquisity#7344 and Acquisity/Acquisity#7398.

## Done when

- [ ] A test fails today and passes after: a refused or busy outbound call leaves the session active and shows Retry call.
- [ ] The session invariant check shows 0 sessions paused by a refusal (13 in the 13 to 19 Oct data).
- [ ] The PR carries desktop and 375 px screenshots of the new bar state.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add the power dialler launch button and session panel
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12173. For THIS ticket: this is the first screen reps SEE of the power dialler. A Call button appears on saved contact and deal views; clicking it starts a session and opens the session panel (open the Close links below for the exact look). The backend already exists by the time this starts; you are wiring UI onto `startSession`, `claimNext`, and `getActiveClaims`. Three things to keep straight: (1) "**being called by \[rep\]**" indicators come from polling `getActiveClaims` every 10-15 seconds, never from the 5-minute sync; (2) show THREE separate counts (rows in the view, unique people with phones, phoneless rows) because deals can share one person and some rows have nobody to call — one blended number would lie; (3) the manual **Next Call** button must work fully on its own, because the auto-advance rhythm ships in the NEXT ticket and QA tests this one standalone. Also: this ticket carries the PostHog usage-tracking requirement (use the repo's `instrument-activation-tracking` skill; done = events visible in PostHog, not just code merged). Why it matters: this is the SDR's daily cockpit.

**Size:** M/L · **Design:** needed (Name 2 CRM page 1444-65385) · **Blocked by:** ENG-12183, ENG-12184, ENG-12186, ENG-12187
**How it should look (Close reference):** the session controls and Call button on a list (images): <url> and <url>

### Overview

A rep opens a saved view (a saved, filtered list of contacts or deals), clicks Call, and a session panel appears. The panel shows who they are about to call, the queue ahead, who else on the team is already on which lead, and a Next Call button. This is the first rep-facing screen of the power dialler.

### Problem

The backend (sessions, queue, claims, safe dialling) exists after ENG-12177 to ENG-12186, but there is no way for a rep to start or drive a session. Nothing is visible in the product.

### Solution

* A Call button at the top of saved contact views AND saved deal views.
* A session panel with: the current lead card, a queue preview with claim indicators ("being called by [rep]"), Pause, a manual Next Call button, a ring-time setting, a caller ID picker, and progress.
* Claim indicators come from polling `dialer.getActiveClaims` every 10 to 15 seconds. The 5 minute view sync can never power this. The server returns only claims on contacts visible in the caller's session and view scope, never all org claims.
* Manual Next Call works standalone: one click claims and dials the next lead through the ENG-12187 hooks. No automation is needed, which makes this ticket independently QA-able before the wrap-up ticket exists.
* Counts are shown as three separate numbers: source rows (rows in the view), unique dialable contacts (deduplicated people who have a phone number), and phoneless (rows with no callable number, surfaced, never silently dropped). Unique dialable contacts is the progress denominator.
* The panel shows a cursor-exhausted state: when the whole list has been loaded into the queue and worked, the rep sees a clear "queue complete" state. This is distinct from "all remaining leads are on calls with teammates, retry shortly", which shows a retry time instead.
* Session state lives in the URL (nuqs), so refresh and deep links restore the panel.
* PostHog activation tracking ships with this ticket, instrumented through the repo `instrument-activation-tracking` skill (never hand-written calls), at least `tool.opened`. Tracking only counts once the events are verified landing in PostHog.

**Technical notes**

* Launch surfaces: saved contact views and saved deal views (deal rows dial the resolved contact per ENG-12183's rule).
* Permission matrix: the button renders only with `FEATURES.POWER_DIALER` plus `voice.make_call`, and every procedure it calls rejects server-side without them, so hiding the UI is never the protection. Claim data is scoped server-side as above.

### Scope

* In: Call button on saved contact and deal views
* In: session panel (current lead, queue preview, claim indicators, Pause, manual Next Call, ring-time setting, caller ID picker, progress with the three count grains)
* In: cursor-exhausted state and leased-elsewhere retry state
* In: URL session state, refresh restore
* In: PostHog activation tracking, verified in PostHog
* Out of scope: wrap-up window and auto-advance (next ticket), Continue Calling chooser UI (next ticket, backend in ENG-12185), recovery and takeover screens (next ticket), voicemail drop (RCC 8)

### Acceptance criteria

 1. When a rep with the feature flag and calling permission opens a saved contact view or a saved deal view, a Call button is shown. Without the flag or permission, the button is absent AND direct calls to the procedures are rejected server-side.
 2. When the rep clicks Call, a session starts and the panel opens showing the current lead's name and number.
 3. When the panel shows progress, source rows, unique dialable contacts, and phoneless are displayed as separate numbers, and the progress denominator is unique dialable contacts.
 4. When another rep in the same shared view is on a lead, the queue shows "being called by [rep]" within 15 seconds.
 5. When the rep clicks Next Call, the next lead is claimed and dialled through the shared calling engine, with no auto-advance required. This works end to end before the wrap-up ticket ships.
 6. When every remaining lead is leased by teammates, the panel shows a retry message with a time, never a false "queue complete".
 7. When the whole list has been loaded and every item worked, the panel shows the complete (cursor-exhausted) state.
 8. When the rep changes ring time or caller ID, the next dials use the new values. Pause stops claiming.
 9. When the rep refreshes the page, the URL restores the session panel.
10. When the dialler is opened, a `tool.opened` event (at minimum) is sent via the repo instrumentation skill and is verified landing in PostHog before this ticket is called done.

### Design (Name 2)

* 27 · power dialer preflight — the launch modal: view name, in-scope / callable / excluded counts, skip reasons ("2 have no phone number, one is on the do-not-call list"), caller ID, queue order, **Start N calls**
* 28 · power dialer active — bottom bar — the session panel while dialling: bottom-docked, current lead + pipeline/stage, call controls, timer, End call

Launch entry point is the **Start Power Dialer** button in the list toolbar (visible in both frames). Full screen map on master ENG-12173.

relatedSnapshot.title: Power Dialer Save and call next does nothing after sending a text
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What's happening

In a Power Dialer session's wrap-up card, opening the **Text** panel stops **Save and call next** from working. Clicking it does nothing — no error, no disabled state, no reason given. It stays dead until the rep taps **Text** again to close the panel or ends the session. Auto-next is stalled the same way. Reported by a rep who hit it repeatedly and had to keep ending sessions and restarting.

## What should happen

The open text panel should hold the automatic auto-next countdown (so a draft isn't lost mid-send), but **Save and call next** should always advance when clicked. Once the text is sent, the panel should close so auto-next can resume.

## Who it hits and how bad

Every rep using the CRM v2 Power Dialer session card who texts a prospect from wrap-up — a core workflow for unanswered calls. They lose their place-flow and think the dialler is broken; one rep ended and restarted sessions multiple times in a day.

## How to see it

1. Start a Power Dialer session in the CRM v2 dialler and finish a call.
2. In wrap-up, tap **Text** under Next step and send a text (or just leave the panel open).
3. Pick an outcome, then click **Save and call next**. Nothing happens.

Slack report (with screenshot): <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>

## What we know so far

Root cause confirmed in code. The wrap-up surface treats the open text composer the same as a modal or a pending save: it sets a flag that feeds the wrap-up hook's `blocked` input. That flag is checked inside the advance guard, so the advance returns early with no error — the button looks enabled but the click is silently swallowed. Auto-next's countdown is held by the same flag. The hold was meant to protect an unsent draft from a surprise auto-advance; blocking the explicit manual click was collateral.

## Done when

- [ ] With the text panel open, clicking **Save and call next** advances to the next call.
- [ ] With the text panel open and auto-next on, the countdown does not fire; after the text is sent the panel closes and auto-next works again.
- [ ] A unit test covers advancing while the composer is open, and the countdown staying held.

<details><summary>For whoever fixes it</summary>

* `apps/web/components/crm-v2/phone/power-dialer-session-wrap-up.tsx` — `textOpen` → `wrap.setComposerOpen(textOpen)`.
* `apps/web/components/crm/power-dialer/use-power-dialer-wrap-up-surface.ts` — `composerOpen` feeds `surfaceBlockedRef` and the `blocked` input.
* `apps/web/components/crm/power-dialer/use-power-dialer-wrap-up.ts` — `blocked` flows into `countdownBlocked`, which `runAdvance`'s `shouldContinue` guard checks; adding a countdown-only hold fixes it.
* `apps/web/components/crm-v2/record/record-composer.tsx` — `ContactTextComposer` already accepts `onSent`; use it to close the panel after a send.
* Tests: `apps/web/tests/components/crm/power-dialer/use-power-dialer-wrap-up.test.tsx`.
* docs/agents file: `docs/agents/telephony.md`.

</details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Power Dialler can ring a person twice before moving on
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep running the Power Dialler can turn on "Ring twice if no answer". When the first call to a person is not answered, the dialler calls them again straight away, once, before moving to the next person. Many people ignore the first call from an unknown number and pick up the second.

## Problem

Asked on the 30 Sep migration call by an SDR in AI Acquisition Sales Team: "Can you double dial with the Power Dialler? Ring up the person twice before moving on to the next lead." Today the Power Dialler calls each person once. To try again the rep has to stop, open the person and call by hand, which breaks the session.

## User experience

* In the Power Dialler session settings, next to ring timeout and auto-advance, there is a switch: **Ring twice if no answer**. It is off by default and remembered per rep.
* With it on, when a call ends without being answered the session card says "No answer. Calling again…" and the second call starts after a short pause, with a Skip button to move on instead.
* If the second call is not answered either, the session carries on as it does today: wrap-up, then the next person.
* If the first call is answered, goes to a voicemail the rep leaves a message on, or the rep ends it and picks an outcome, there is no second call.
* Both calls appear on the person's timeline as separate calls, and both count in the session summary as attempts. The person counts once.

## What's included

* The switch, the "calling again" state on the session card with Skip, and the second call.
* Not included: more than two attempts, a second attempt on a different number for the same person, and double dial for single calls made outside the Power Dialler.

## How it should work

* The second call goes through the same checks as any call: do not contact, opt-out, contact hours, phone funds and the rep's caller ID. If a check fails, the session moves on and says why.
* The person stays claimed by this rep between the two calls, so no other rep's session can pick them up in the gap.
* Pausing or ending the session during the gap cancels the second call.
* "Continue calling" still skips people attempted in the last hour, counting either attempt.

## Done when

- [ ] With the switch on, an unanswered first call is followed by one second call to the same person, and an unanswered second call moves on.
- [ ] An answered first call, or one the rep ends with an outcome, is not followed by a second call.
- [ ] Skip during the pause moves to the next person without calling again.
- [ ] With the switch off, the Power Dialler behaves exactly as today.
- [ ] A person marked do not contact between the two calls is not called again.
- [ ] Two reps running sessions on the same view never both call the person during the gap.
- [ ] Both calls show on the person's timeline, and the session summary counts two attempts and one person.
- [ ] Use of the switch is tracked through the repo's activation tracking skill, and the event is verified landing in PostHog.
- [ ] Live-call QA with a test number that does not answer, and one that answers on the second call.

## Open questions

* **What counts as "no answer".** Recommended default: the call ended without connecting (no answer, busy, or the ring timeout was reached). A carrier voicemail that picks up counts as answered, so it is not redialled, because the rep is already on the line with it.
* **Pause before the second call.** Recommended default: 3 seconds, not configurable.

## Implementation context

* Session settings today are auto-advance (on or off; 5, 10, 15 or 30 seconds) in `apps/web/lib/dialer/preferences.ts`, stored per rep per workspace in `dialer_user_preference`, and the ring timeout in `apps/web/lib/dialer/ring-timeout.ts`. The new switch belongs with them.
* The next person is claimed in `apps/web/lib/dialer/claim-next.ts` and an item is finished in `complete-item.ts`. The second attempt needs the item to stay claimed and not complete after the first unanswered call.
* Dial checks live in `authorize-dial.ts`, `dial-suppression.ts` and `do-not-contact-call.ts` and must run again for the second call.
* The session summary's no-answer counting is in `session-summary.ts`.
* A new column on `dialer_user_preference` is a small schema change.

relatedSnapshot.title: Power dialler: a refused or busy balance check pauses the session instead of offering Retry call
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What's happening

When a power dialler call is refused by the phone balance check (including "your phone balance is being checked" and "balance check expired"), the whole session is paused and labelled as paused by the user. The bar then says "Waiting for the server to confirm the call outcome…" and offers no Retry call, so reps end the session and start a new one. Part of ENG-15734 (dialler reliability, Wave 0, item 0.5).

Measured 13 to 19 Oct 2026: 33 dials refused in the Twilio answer step, 13 of them balance-check refusals. One rep had 17 refusals in 3 hours and started 7 sessions.

## Cause

* `apps/web/lib/dialer/authorize-dial.ts` pauses the session on any `CallFundingError` with `pausedReason: 'user'`.
* `apps/web/components/crm/power-dialer/controller-state.ts` records a dial-start failure only when the ended call has no CallSid. A refusal in the answer step has one, so the item stays claimed with no Retry.

## What should happen

A refused or busy call leaves the session active and the bar shows Retry call for the same contact.

## Done when

* A unit test on controller-state shows a failed dialler call with a CallSid on a still-claimed item is retryable (fails today).
* A refused funding check no longer pauses the session (test fails today).

Related: ENG-15734, ENG-15739, ENG-15577.

relatedSnapshot.title: Run the power dialler on each lead's record, from any smart view
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

A rep opens any smart view on People, presses **Power dialler** and works the list one person at a time, on each person's own record. The call sits in a bar at the top, the person's context fills the page under it, and the outcomes stay in the same place on the right. Anyone can add six ready-made calling lists, such as New leads and No-shows, from New smart view in one click: for themselves, or for the whole team if they're an admin.

Clickable designs: Power dialler designs (15 Oct 2026). Use the State menu at the bottom right to step through every state; add `&role=member` to a link to see what a non-admin sees, or `&amd=on` for answer detection on. It's private until James shares it from the page's Share menu.

## Why

Part of ENG-15216: this is where reps start and run a session.

* This replaces the Calling page this ticket used to describe. James reviewed the designs on 15 Oct 2026 and chose no separate page: reps should see each lead's full context as they're dialled, the way Close does, and starting from a smart view has to be obvious.
* Today the session is a card on the People or Deals list, so a rep in a session never sees the record of the person they're calling. Aaron's ENG-15235 asks for the profile to open when a call connects, and this delivers that outcome.
* Starting is hard today: 14 of 16 team People views can't start the dialler at all (ENG-15236), which is why that ticket blocks this one.
* No-shows were the busiest list in the 30 days to 12 Oct 2026, with 3,957 calls against 2,541 for booked calls, but reps have to build a view by hand to work them.
* ENG-15217 shipped on 14 Oct 2026 (outcome gate, 1.5 s Undo, keys, Skip, honest voicemail wording). This ticket moves those behaviours onto the record and restyles them; it doesn't rebuild them.

## How it should work

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    A[Saved view on People or Deals] --> B[Start] --> C[Session card on the list]
    C -. rep opens the record .-> D[Session card is gone]
  end
  subgraph After
    E[Any smart view, or an added calling list] --> F[Power dialler 34] --> G[Person's own record: call bar, brief, outcomes]
    G -- outcome saved, 1.5 s Undo --> H[Next person's record, already loaded]
    G -- End session --> I[Session summary]
  end
```

### People, any smart view

* The button reads **Power dialler** with the number of callable people in a green pill ("Power dialler 34"). Hovering says "Calls the 34 people in Qualified this month one after another. Each person's brief opens before they pick up." On a phone it shrinks to the icon and count.
* The arrow next to it opens: **Continue calling** ("From Name 101, 7 of 34. Stopped at 11:40 am."), **Start from scratch**, and **Settings for this session**.
* Settings for this session holds Ring twice, a line saying whether answer detection is on or off and what a voicemail will do (linking to Phone settings), Caller ID, and the ring time. The ring time shown is the session's real setting (32 s by default), not a fixed number.
* When the view can't be called, the button is disabled with the reason and a fix link, as ENG-15217 already does.

### New smart view, Calling lists tab

* New smart view gets a third tab next to AI view and Manual filters: **Calling lists** (People, for everyone). Going back is one click on AI view.
* Above the cards, **Add as Personal or Team**. Everyone can add a list as Personal, which only they see. Admins can also pick Team, which everyone on the team sees in Views. Members see Personal only, with "Admins can add lists for the whole team."
* The AI view's empty state shows "Or start from a ready-made calling list" with the three busiest lists and a "See all six calling lists" link. The left column has the same link under its own heading, and the Views menu keeps "Calling list · ready-made".
* Six cards: New leads, Due now, No-shows, Missed calls, Unconfirmed and Today's calls. Each says who is in it and in what order, the live count, and the oldest wait. **Add** creates a normal view (Personal or Team) and opens it, so Power dialler dials it. A list that's already added reads "Added · Open".
* Footer: "A list skips anyone another rep is on the phone with, anyone marked Do not contact and anyone without a phone."
* The lists' rules run on the server, because some aren't filters (a missed inbound call, no reply to a confirmation text). Missed calls reads the missed inbound calls that ENG-12494 surfaces.
* **Exits:** Do not call, Wrong number, Not interested, Lost and Closed remove a person from every list. Missed calls exits on any connected outbound call or a Called back outcome. No-shows exits on Rebooked, Lost or a new appointment.
* **One eligibility time per person,** checked when claimed and when dialled, so switching lists can't get round the team-wide 60-minute redial gap.

### The session, on the person's record

* **Session strip** (one slim row): the view and position ("Qualified this month, 7 of 34") with a progress line, then Calls, Connected and rate, Booked, Talk and Session time, Up next, the keys list and an outlined **End session**.
* **Call bar:** the one coloured thing on the page. It's white in the preview and wrap-up, and pale green only while ringing or live. It shows the name large, company and title, their local time, phone, attempt, status in words ("Name 5 in 3 s", "No answer, ringing again (2 of 2)"), the timer, and the controls: Mute, Drop voicemail (V), Pause after this one, and a red hang up. While a call is live and recording is on, a **Recording** label with a red dot sits at the top of the session.
* **Under the bar:** the lead brief (ENG-15465), with the Activity and Details tabs one click away.
* **Right column:** the outcome panel, always in the same place. Before a call it's disabled with "Outcomes open when Name 6 picks up". Under it, a **Next up** card for the person after this one.
* A 3-second preview before each dial. Today's calls is preview only: the rep starts each call.
* Moving on opens the next person's record, which is loaded before the current call ends, so there's no wait.
* No black in the session: Call now, Next now and Resume are soft green, End session is outlined, hang up is red.

### End session

A summary: calls, connected and rate, booked, session time and talk time, and each person called with their outcome. **Keep calling** goes back to the session; closing returns to the view.

### Calling settings the session has to respect

Both cases of each setting must work. Values for our sales team's workspace are from the read-only replica on 15 Oct 2026.

| Setting | Our sales team today | When on | When off |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Answer detection (whole workspace) | Off | A machine answer hangs up before the beep, logs "Voicemail, no message", skips wrap-up and moves on. | The rep hears the voicemail and presses V or picks Voicemail. |
| Ring twice (per rep) | On for all 5 reps | Re-rings only when nobody picked up or the line was busy, never a voicemail. | One ring per person. |
| Automatic next call (per rep) | On, 5 s | The outcome gate and 1.5 s Undo from ENG-15217. | The rep presses Next (N). |
| Ring time (per session) | 32 s default | Shown in session settings as set. |  |
| Recording by default (workspace) | On | A Recording label shows while the call is live. | No label. |

Answer detection was on for 2,662 outbound calls in the 30 days to 15 Oct 2026: 1,390 came back as a machine, 503 as a person, and 769 had no clear answer, which the session treats as a person.

### Manager floor

Next to rep status, each calling list shows how many people are waiting and the oldest wait.

## Design

James approved these on 15 Oct 2026. Kit screens, light theme, 1440 wide:

 <image> 

The states after a call (waiting for an outcome, paused while typing, Next with Undo, keys, and voicemail with answer detection on and off) render in the new layout like this:

 <image> 

## Decisions already made

* No separate Calling page. A session always starts from a smart view or an added calling list.
* Calling lists are normal views. Anyone can add one as Personal; admins can also add one for the Team (James, 15 Oct 2026). They're renamed, pinned or deleted from Views like any other view.
* The session shows a Recording label while a recorded call is live (James, 15 Oct 2026).
* The button says Power dialler, whether the session is new or unfinished. Continue calling lives in its menu.
* The call bar is the only tinted surface, and it's green only while a call rings or is live.
* Ring twice never re-rings a voicemail, whether it was detected or heard.

## Not doing

* What's inside the lead brief: ENG-15465.
* What each outcome does after the call: ENG-15221.
* Attempt schedules and calling hours: ENG-15222.
* Leaving a recorded voicemail: ENG-12188.
* Fixing the views that can't start the dialler: ENG-15236.

## Open questions

* **Should** ENG-15235 **close once this ships?** Recommended: yes, because the record is on screen for every call in a session. Aaron and James decide.

## Done when

- [ ] From any team People view that passes the dialler preflight, Power dialler starts a session on the first person's record, with no extra setup.
- [ ] Each next person opens on their own record within a second of the Undo window closing, with the call bar and outcome panel in the same place.
- [ ] Adding a calling list from New smart view creates a view, Power dialler dials it, and the card then reads "Added · Open".
- [ ] A member can add a calling list only as Personal, and nobody else sees it. An admin can add one as Team, and every teammate sees it in Views.
- [ ] With default recording on, a live call shows the Recording label; with it off, no label shows.
- [ ] A person marked Do not call or Wrong number never appears in any calling list.
- [ ] A person called by anyone in the last 60 minutes isn't dialled from any list.
- [ ] With answer detection on, a machine answer logs "Voicemail, no message" and moves on. With it off, the rep hears the voicemail and can press V or pick Voicemail. A test covers both.
- [ ] Ring twice re-rings a no answer once and never re-rings a voicemail.
- [ ] End session shows the summary with counts that match the calls placed.
- [ ] The manager floor shows each calling list's oldest wait.
- [ ] PostHog receives `tool.opened` for the Calling lists tab and `dialler.session_started` with the view or list name.

<details><summary>For whoever builds it</summary>

* Code at commit 28fcbd9b55: the session card is `apps/web/components/crm-v2/phone/power-dialer-session-card.tsx`, mounted from `apps/web/components/crm/power-dialer/power-dialer-workspace.tsx`, which People (`people-table.tsx`) and Deals (`deals-kanban.tsx`) render. Moving the session onto the record means the record route owns it.

The screens are `crm-call-session.tsx`, `crm-call-queues.tsx` (Power dialler button and menu), `crm-calling-lists.tsx` (the six cards) and `crm-list-controls.tsx` (New smart view's Calling lists tab). relatedSnapshot.title: Create the database tables for power dialler sessions, queues, and locks
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12173. For THIS ticket: the **power dialler** lets a rep press Call on a list and the system dials person after person. Several reps will run it at the same time on the SAME list, so we need database-level guarantees that two reps never phone the same person at once, even if browsers crash mid-call. This ticket is pure schema: four new tables and their unique constraints. A "**lease**" here is a short-lived lock row saying "this person is being dialled by rep X right now" (like an inventory reservation during checkout: nobody else can take the item while the reservation lives). The "**live call registry**" is a row per phone call actually in progress, so we never treat someone as free while a rep is mid-conversation with them. No UI, no logic, just Drizzle schema + migration. Why it matters: every other power dialler ticket builds on these tables, so this is deliberately first and deliberately small.

**Size:** M · **Design:** none · **Blocked by:** nothing
**How it should work (Close reference):** the power dialler overall: <url>

### Overview

When an SDR starts power dialling a list, the system needs to remember their run: which view it came from, who is in the queue, who they are calling now, and which leads other reps are already on. This ticket creates that storage. Reps see nothing new yet. Every other power dialler ticket builds on these tables, so this starts on day one.

### Problem

There are no dialler tables in the database today. There is nowhere to store a calling session, a calling queue, or a lock that stops two reps dialling the same person at the same time.

### Solution

Add four new tables. In plain terms:

* A **session** table: one row per calling run (which view, current status, settings).
* A **session item** table: one row per person in that run's queue.
* A **lease** table. A lease is a short-lived lock marking a lead as being dialled by one rep, so nobody else dials them at the same time.
* A **live call registry**: a list of calls happening right now, so the system never treats a lead as free while someone is actually talking to them.

Technical notes (fields are exact, from the approved data model):

* New file `packages/db/src/schema/dialer.ts` plus migration.
* `dialer_session`: `id`, `organizationId`, `memberId`, `viewId` (FK to `crm_view`, ON DELETE SET NULL), `viewName` (copied name, survives view deletion), `entityType` (contact|deal), `filterSnapshot`/`sortSnapshot` jsonb (sort is authoritative; filters are re-read live at sync), `status` (active|paused|completed|abandoned), `pausedReason` (user|view_deleted|access_lost), `controllerToken` + `controllerGeneration` (a controller token is a secret marking which browser tab may drive the session; it rotates on takeover), `materializationCursor` (a bookmark: last sort key plus id tie-breaker, recording how far the queue has been built from the view), `callerId`, `ringTimeoutSec` (default 32), `mode` (continue|fresh), `materializedCount`, `totalCount`, `lastSyncedAt`, `startedAt`, `endedAt`, `lastActivityAt` (input for the idle sweep), `wrapUpDeadline` (server-owned; wrap-up ends the lease when it passes).
* One active-or-paused session per rep, enforced in the database: partial unique index on `memberId` WHERE `status IN ('active','paused')`. A second session is blocked even if the UI misbehaves.
* `dialer_session_item`: `id`, `sessionId`, `contactId` (the canonical resolved contact, always set), `entityId` (the representative entity: contact or deal id), `sourceEntityIds` jsonb (all qualifying deals that share this contact), `position` (gapped numeric), `status` (pending|deferred|claimed|completed|skipped|removed), `phoneSnapshot`, `callSid` (bound at dial, idempotent), `crmEventId`, `dispositionCopy` (display only; `call.disposition` stays the authority), `completedAt`. Unique on `(sessionId, contactId)`: the same person can never appear twice in one session's queue.
* `dialer_contact_lease`: `organizationId`, `contactId`, `memberId`, `sessionId`, `sessionItemId`, `acquiredAt`, `leaseExpiresAt` (DB `now()` + ~3 minutes). UNIQUE on `(organizationId, contactId)`: one lock per person per organization, across every view and session.
* `dialer_live_call`: `callSid` (primary key), `organizationId`, `sessionId`, `sessionItemId`, `contactId`, `memberId`, `state` (dialing|ringing|connected), `lastCallbackAt`, `startedAt`. Set at dial, updated by status callbacks, row deleted on the terminal callback.
* Indexes for the known access patterns: sessions by member and status, items by session plus status plus position, leases by expiry, live calls by `lastCallbackAt` (watchdog scan).

### Scope

* In: the four tables, fields, constraints, and indexes above; the migration; schema exports.
* In: database-enforced rules: one active-or-paused session per rep, unique item per `(sessionId, contactId)`, unique lease per `(organizationId, contactId)`.
* Out of scope: any procedures, business logic, or UI. Session lifecycle, claiming, and view sync are separate tickets. No new endpoints here, so permission enforcement lands with the procedures.

### Acceptance criteria

1. When the migration runs on a fresh database and on a copy of an existing one, then it applies cleanly and changes no existing table data.
2. When a rep already has an active or paused session and a second session row is inserted for the same member, then the database rejects it.
3. When a completed or abandoned session exists for a rep, then a new session for that rep inserts fine (the unique rule only covers active and paused).
4. When two items with the same `(sessionId, contactId)` are inserted, then the database rejects the second.
5. When two leases for the same `(organizationId, contactId)` are inserted, then the database rejects the second.
6. When a saved view is deleted, then sessions pointing at it keep their row: `viewId` becomes null and `viewName` still holds the copied name.

relatedSnapshot.title: Stop two reps calling the same person from click-to-call or inbound
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Part of ENG-15216. Power sessions already hold a person for 3 minutes and show "Being called by" to other reps, but click-to-call and inbound calls ignore that hold. So two reps can still ring the same person. This extends the hold to every call, so a lead never gets two reps at once.

## Problem

* Click-to-call checks do-not-contact, caller ID and outbound policy, but never reads or takes the per-person hold.
* Answering an inbound call doesn't take the hold either.
* The hold is keyed on the contact, so two contact records with the same phone number slip through.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    P[Power session] -- takes hold --> L[(Per-person hold)]
    C[Click-to-call] -. ignores .-> L
    I[Inbound answer] -. ignores .-> L
  end
  subgraph After
    P2[Power session] --> L2[(Hold on contact and phone)]
    C2[Click-to-call] -- takes or warns --> L2
    I2[Inbound answer] -- takes --> L2
  end
```

## What's included

* **One hold on contact and phone:** the contact and the normalised phone number (scoped to the workspace) are held together in one transaction, or not at all.
* **Click-to-call:** it takes the hold. If someone else holds it, the rep sees "Name 7 is calling now" with Call anyway. Calling anyway asks for a short reason and is logged.
* **Inbound:** never blocked. Answering takes the hold if it's free. If a power session holds it idle, inbound takes over and that session skips the person. If an outbound call is live, inbound still connects and both reps see a badge.
* **Renewal:** the hold renews while the call is live or in wrap-up, and releases on the saved outcome or after 3 idle minutes.
* **Visibility:** a "calling now" badge on the person and deal pages.
* **Overrides:** admins and managers can release an idle hold; nobody can end a live call through this. Every override and release is logged.
* **Tracking:** send `lock.override` to PostHog after a successful Call anyway or authorized idle-hold release. Include the workspace, acting rep, affected contact and action. Keep the existing audit reason; analytics failure must not prevent calling or releasing a hold.

### Follow-up from the wrap-up PR

Also covers two findings from Acquisity/Acquisity#7156:

* **Next shortcut:** N must respect the same safety blockers as the Next/Retry button, including unsaved caller ID or ring time and pending session controls. It must recheck those blockers before placing a call.
* **Start repair actions:** when Start is blocked by an unsaved view or view changes, offer the relevant Save/Reset action. Calling settings is the repair destination for caller-ID/setup problems; feature or access restrictions should give the appropriate admin guidance.

The shortcut gap was confirmed in the reviewed code and an isolated handler replay. Acquisity/Acquisity#7156 has since merged. Both the shortcut and Start repair gaps remain present on the main revision reviewed on 14 October 2026 and are covered here. Reproduction and the updated minimal implementation plan are in the existing AI context document.

## Done when

* With rep A in a power session holding a person, rep B's click-to-call shows the warning, and calling anyway writes a logged override. How to check: a two-rep test.
* Two contact records sharing a phone can't be rung by two reps at once. How to check: a test with duplicate records.
* Answering an inbound call while another rep's session holds the person idle makes that session skip them.
* A rep who isn't an admin or manager can't release someone else's hold.
* Call anyway and authorized idle-hold releases produce `lock.override` in PostHog during a two-rep preview test. Retries do not create duplicate events, and denied or canceled actions do not count as successful overrides.
* With an unapplied caller-ID or ring-time change, both Next/Retry and N stay blocked on both existing dialler screens. After Apply succeeds, N uses the saved settings. Pending controls and paused sessions cannot be bypassed.
* Every Start blocker offers a repair action or admin guidance matching its reason. A view blocker does not send the rep to Calling settings.

## Implementation context

Refreshed 14 October 2026 against main at e2127713d6 and production read-only schema/aggregate inspection on a replica. Existing Power Dialer leases are session-only; the shared `call` table already covers actual inbound/outbound calls. The minimal plan reuses both, adds two nullable hold fields to `call`, and uses one transactional contact/normalized-phone admission check. No new reservation table or session-lease generalization. Extend the existing 60-minute Power Dialer recent-call check to recognize duplicate phone records while preserving its duration and explicit Ring again behavior. The full implementation, guardrails and ticket coverage are recorded in AI context.md.

`lock.override` tracking is owned here, moved from ENG-15217. AI context.md records the existing tracking helper, source PR and focused verification approach.

relatedSnapshot.title: Show a lead brief for each person the power dialler calls
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What we want

As each person comes up in a power dialler session, the rep sees one brief, built from the person's record, that answers five questions before the call connects: who is this, why am I calling now, what happened last, where's the money, and what did they say. Nothing is clicked or typed per person, and the next person's brief is ready before the rep gets to them.

## Why

Part of ENG-15216: this fills the record page that ENG-15220 puts the session on.

* Today the session card shows one line, "Last touch 20 minutes ago", with no name, channel or note (ENG-15159). A rep who connects has to click around for context while the person is talking.
* James asked for this on 15 Oct 2026: SDRs and setters should find all the context they need on the lead they're dialling, shown automatically for each lead.
* Reps make 9.5 calls a day each on our dialler against 43.9 on Close (30 days to 12 Oct 2026). A brief that's ready on pick-up removes the reason to check the record before every dial.

## How it should work

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    A[Session card] --> B[Last touch, no name] --> C[Rep opens the record mid-call]
  end
  subgraph After
    D[Person comes up] --> E[Brief built from the record, already loaded] --> F[Why now, Last touch, Deal and money, What they said]
    D --> G[Next 2 people loaded, AI summary ready]
  end
```

### Lead brief, at the top of the record during a session

Five groups, each filled from data we already store:

1. **Why now.** One reason pill and the one thing to read. Reasons are checked in this order: they wrote or called in and nobody answered (quoting their words, for example "Name 8 today 10:15"), a task due or overdue, a booked meeting coming up, then a failed or processing payment. In a calling list session, the list's own reason wins the pill ("Registered 2 h ago"), and their latest unanswered message is still the quote. Under the quote:
   * **Answer on this call:** any question in their messages.
   * **Also:** the other reasons, in quiet text.
   * **AI summary,** already open.
2. **Last touch.** The newest call, the last message we sent, the last note and the last past meeting, each with who, when and its result.
3. **Deal and money.** The open deal, its stage, value and next step. Then paid against the contract, the amount owed, processing and failed payments, and the last payment. Then open tasks on the person and on their deals, which the record timeline misses today.
4. **What they said.** Their messages, newest first, leaving out the one already quoted, then qualification fields (budget, decision maker, timeline) or form answers.
5. **Activity and Details tabs.** The full timeline and every field, one click away.

An empty group says so in words, for example "No deal yet. Booking a call creates one." A person with nothing on the record shows "Nobody has spoken to Name 9 yet. Open with who you are and why you're calling."

### Next up card

The right column shows the person after this one, with their reason and their brief already built.

### Loading

The briefs for the current person and the next two are loaded before their dial, and their AI summaries are generated ahead, so nothing loads after the person picks up.

## Design

James approved these on 15 Oct 2026. Clickable: Power dialler designs, private until James shares it. Kit screens, light theme, 1440 wide:

 <image> 

## Decisions already made

* The brief only reads data we already store. No new fields.
* The AI summary uses the existing record summary (ENG-13791), not a new model call per group.
* The Why now order above is fixed. A calling list's own reason wins the pill.
* Upcoming meetings show under Also, not under Last touch.
* Summaries are generated ahead only when the stored one is older than 24 hours or the record has new activity since it was written. We read the cost after the first week (James, 15 Oct 2026).

## Not doing

* The session layout, call bar and moving between people: ENG-15220.
* The warning before a manual dial when a teammate called recently: ENG-15218 and ENG-15159.
* What outcomes do: ENG-15221.

## Open questions

* **How do we find "Answer on this call"?** Recommended: have the record summary return the open questions in the same call, so there's one model call per person. Anuj decides, with James.
* **The AI summary often repeats the next step shown under Deal and money.** Recommended: tell the summary to leave out what the brief already shows. Anuj decides.

## Done when

- [ ] In a session, the current person's brief is on screen when their preview opens, with no click, and never later than 2 seconds after the call is answered.
- [ ] Why now picks the right reason for each case (unanswered message, task due, meeting coming up, payment problem, calling list reason). A unit test covers each.
- [ ] Open tasks on the person's deals show under Deal and money.
- [ ] A person with nothing on the record shows the empty words, and the layout keeps its shape.
- [ ] Next up shows the following person with their brief already built.
- [ ] PostHog receives `tool.opened` for the brief.

<details><summary>For whoever builds it</summary>

* Design kit (private frontend library, branch `power-dialler-design-2026-10-12`): `buildBrief({ lead, shell, queueReason })` and `LeadBriefCard` in `crm-call-brief.tsx`. The kit fixtures use real record shapes, so the grouping logic ports directly.
* Existing data at commit 28fcbd9b55: record summary in `apps/web/trpc/routers/crm/record-summary.ts` and `apps/web/components/crm-v2/record/record-summary.tsx`; payments in `apps/web/components/crm-v2/payments/payments-model.ts`; latest communication with the rep's name in `apps/web/lib/crm/latest-communication-registry.ts`.
* Related: ENG-15235 (profile on connect), ENG-15237 (the call note on the profile), ENG-15159.

</details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Power Dialer never rings a second time when Ring twice if no answer is on
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What's happening

With **Ring twice if no answer** switched on in the Power Dialer, the second call never happens. When a call rings out unanswered, the dialer skips straight to the next person instead of ringing again.

Reported by Name 10 in Slack: thread

## What should happen

When a dialer call ends with no answer, the rep gets the "Calling again in 3s" prompt and the person is rung a second time before the dialer moves on — including when the rep has already logged the wrap-up outcome (which is mandatory to move on).

## Root cause (confirmed from prod data + code, Name 11 19 Oct)

* **Call outcomes are not being recorded wrong.** The \~50 `unknown` dispositions in Name 3's history are answered calls (answered_at set, real talk durations) where machine detection is off — `unknown` is the deliberate classification for "completed call, detection disabled". His `no_answer` calls are classified correctly and every call has an outcome_id. The earlier "never picked up" reading was wrong.
* **The outcome gate made the retry unreachable.** (1) Client: `confirmOutcome` called `cancelRingAgain()` after saving, killing the countdown. (2) Server: `ringDialerItemAgain` required `call.outcomeId === null`. Since the rep can't advance without logging an outcome, ring-again could essentially never fire.

The manual re-dial reason prompt is by design (the person is still held by the caller's own wrap-up) — confirmed working as intended, separate UX question.

## Fix (PR open)

<url:github.com> — outcome save no longer cancels the countdown and the server no longer requires a null outcomeId. Disposition `no_answer`/`busy` + non-manual source still required; Skip/end-session remains the opt-out. **Note for review:** this reverses deliberate behavior from the original ring-twice work (ENG-14604) — an outcome pick used to suppress the retry.

## Done when

- [X] Root cause confirmed from production evidence
- [ ] With **Ring twice if no answer** on, an unanswered first attempt shows "Calling again in 3s" and places a second call without the rep doing anything
- [X] Decided + documented: the retry still fires after the rep logs a wrap-up outcome (outcome attaches to attempt one; Skip opts out)
- [ ] Real call verified on a calling-enabled workspace (QA)

<details><summary>Code pointers</summary>

* `apps/web/lib/dialer/ring-again.ts` — `ringDialerItemAgain` eligibility check.
* `apps/web/components/crm/power-dialer/use-power-dialer-wrap-up-surface.ts` — `confirmOutcome` (was calling `cancelRingAgain`).
* `apps/web/lib/voice/answer-detection.ts` — `resolveDetectedCallDisposition` (AMD-off completed → `unknown`, deliberate).
* Tests: `apps/web/tests/lib/dialer/ring-again-db.test.ts` (updated), `use-power-dialer-controller-ring-again.test.tsx`.

</details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Company Three workspace: 12 DFY sending mailboxes stuck failed since 2026-09-09 need re-provisioning
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: on 2026-09-24 the Company Three workspace operator (Name 15, <email>) escalated after AI troubleshooting. She reported (1) test campaign emails and her replies never appeared in the AI SDR Inbox and the AI SDR never responded, (2) bounce-backs and emails not sending even though she believed the lead lists were Acquisity-verified, (3) a campaign showing 12 selected sending accounts as "No email accounts connected". She paused both running campaigns pending an answer.

## Human action needed

The workspace is running with 12 dead sending mailboxes.

* Organization: Company Three (org <uuid>)
* 48 DFY mailboxes in total: 36 active/connected, 12 in `status = error`, `connected = false`, `connection_error = "Domain or mailbox provisioning failed"`, created 2026-09-09.
* The 12: <email> / <email> / <email> on <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>.
* Cause: the DFY cold-mail order for those domains reported FAILED at the provider (apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/mail/process-create-order.ts, the domain/mailbox poll marks the domain failed and writes the mailboxes as error). There is no provisioning re-run for that state, so the mailboxes have stayed broken for two weeks.
* Proposed action: re-provision or replace the 12 mailboxes for the workspace, or confirm with the operator that they can be removed. No customer data or money is at stake.

## Verified alongside (no action required)

* The AI SDR reply path is working in this workspace: 20 inbox threads, replies from Cold Email Agent campaigns ingested and processed on 9/15, 9/18 and 9/24, AI replies sent, one meeting booked, no webhook processing errors in outreach_webhook_event.
* The operator's test method cannot reach the inbox. The campaign "Send test email" action posts a standalone provider test (POST /emails/test) whose payload carries no campaign attribution (apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/outreach/send-test-email/child/build-attempt.ts builds eaccount/recipients/subject/bodyHtml only; apps/web/lib/outreach/Company One/client.ts sendTestEmail). AI SDR reply ingestion requires a campaign (apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/data-normalizer.ts normalizeWebhookData returns CAMPAIGN_NOT_FOUND without one; the reply route only fires for reply_received / auto_reply_received). No campaign lead row exists for any of the operator's own addresses in the workspace, so no test send ever went through a campaign. Testing must use a real campaign send to a lead address.
* Bounce-backs: Cohort 1 sent 276 and bounced 12 (4.3%) between 9/18 and 9/24. Its lead list was hand-uploaded (campaign metadata csvUploadStats + lead metadata manuallyAdded), not drawn from the Acquisity lead database, so Acquisity verification never applied to it. Cohort 2's list was uploaded the same way. The Acquisity-sourced list (Cohort 4, 489 leads with scrape metadata) never sent anything.

## Not verified

* The exact on-screen state behind the customer's "12 accounts selected / No email accounts connected" screenshot. No campaign in the workspace lists any of the 12 failed mailboxes in its account selection (campaigns select the 6 or 12 healthy Company Two/Company Two addresses), so the warning most likely came from the account picker listing the workspace's broken DFY mailboxes rather than from a campaign's stored selection.

## Screenshot evidence, read after the first write

The nine screenshots confirm the workspace and sharpen two points.

* Workspace: Company Three; AI SDR status Active with "Process incoming replies" on; assigned call handler Name 16. Three campaigns existed at the time (Cohort 1, 2, 3), which matches production for that moment.
* The test itself: the operator replied from her personal address (<email>) in Gmail at 12:43 on 9/24 to the campaign email "Name 17 x Company Three" sent by the campaign's sending identity, and that campaign email is addressed to a different person (the lead, salutation "Hi Aaron"). A reply that does not come from the campaign's lead address never becomes a campaign reply, so the AI SDR never saw it. That is the same mechanism as the standalone test send, and it replaces the guess that the test-send feature was the only path she used.
* Her third point is real: the Cohort 2 Options tab showed 12 selected accounts, each with a healthy green indicator, next to "No email accounts connected. Add one to start sending." Cohort 2 then sent 72 emails later that day, so the warning was stale rather than predictive. It did not block sending and is worth a product look, not a support action.
* Her original question is answered by design: the referral card says the AI cannot switch contacts on its own yet and offers Resume AI SDR or Stay with Melody.

## What we want

Make the power dialler the fastest way for setters, closers and confirmation reps to work their leads, so more new leads get called, more people show up and fewer inbound calls are missed. A rep presses Power dialler on any smart view and works the list on each person's own record, with a brief that answers why they're calling before the person picks up.

## Why

Since we moved our own sales team off Close, reps have used the power dialler once (one session, 28 Sep 2026). They make 9.5 calls a rep a day by clicking to call one lead at a time, against 43.9 on Close. All figures below are for our sales team's workspace, 13 Sep to 12 Oct 2026, from read-only production queries.

* **New leads go uncalled.** 4,534 of 7,520 new leads with a phone (60.3%) got no outbound call, and the ones called waited a median of 47.8 hours. Only 24 were called within 5 minutes.
* **Inbound callers are missed.** 185 of 242 inbound calls weren't answered.
* **Logging doesn't stick.** 3,206 of 3,371 auto-created call tasks are still open, and only 34 of 26,136 calls carry a deal.
* **Voicemail eats the day.** 54.3% of 2,111 calls since 18 Sep hit voicemail, and reps spent 13.2 hours listening to greetings.

This programme keeps the dialler we built and fixes what stops reps using it.

What changes for reps when everything here ships: a rep opens any smart view, or one of six ready-made calling lists (New leads, Due now, No-shows, Missed calls, Unconfirmed, Today's calls), and presses Power dialler. Each person opens on their own record with the call bar on top, a brief saying why now, what happened last, the money and what they said, and the outcomes on the right. Picking an outcome books, re-queues or moves the deal, then moves on after 1.5 s with Undo, never mid-note. New leads ring an available setter within minutes, unanswered inbound calls ring the rest of the team, and booked calls are confirmed by text before anyone calls.

Power sessions already hold each person for 3 minutes and show "Being called by" to other reps, with a team-wide 60-minute redial gap. The programme keeps that and extends it to every call.

## Decisions already made

* No separate Calling page. Sessions start from a smart view or an added calling list, and run on each person's record (James, 15 Oct 2026).
* Calling lists are normal views with rules that run on the server. Anyone can add one for themselves; admins can add one for the team.
* AI summaries for the lead brief are only regenerated when over 24 hours old or after new activity, and the cost is read after the first week.
* No parallel or predictive dialling. Our leads are fresh, and our research found the evidence favours one line per rep for warm leads.
* The session must work with answer detection on or off, and with each rep's Ring twice and automatic next call settings. ENG-15220 has the table.

## Not doing

* Local presence and number rotation. There's no independent evidence they raise pickups, so we'll revisit once tracking shows connect rate by number.
* Who works no-shows. Calling lists are added per team, so that's a floor decision, not a build.
